bull.b: The Anthropic agreement creates substantial long-duration revenue visibility and expands TeraWulf beyond bitcoin mining into AI infrastructure. A large contracted deployment can support asset utilization, improve planning confidence, and provide a foundation for scaling data-center capacity over several years.

Rapid growth in HPC leasing indicates that the company is converting its power and data-center platform into a recurring infrastructure revenue stream. The increasing mix of lease revenue may make the business less dependent on bitcoin mining economics as additional contracted capacity becomes operational.

The substantial liquidity position and planned Abernathy proceeds give TeraWulf funding capacity for committed construction and near-term expansion. Monetizing a joint-venture interest also supports management’s stated strategy of redeploying capital toward larger, more controlled infrastructure assets.

bear.b: Severe bottom-line losses show that gross profitability is not yet sufficient to cover operating costs and other charges. Unless new HPC capacity improves earnings meaningfully, continued losses could weaken internal funding ability and make the transition to a sustainable business model more difficult.

Material negative operating and free cash flow indicates that the core business is not currently self-funding its operations and investment program. Sustained cash burn increases reliance on project financing, asset monetization, or other capital sources and can limit flexibility if development spending remains elevated.

Very high leverage relative to equity and the reported zero TTM equity base indicate limited balance-sheet support for the company’s debt obligations. This weak capitalization reduces financial flexibility, increases sensitivity to operating setbacks, and may constrain future investment or financing choices.
